To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a disorganized magnetic field can produce a jet-like structure in an MHD turbulent flow; and (ii) the jet-like structures in protostellar disks can be driven by the mean field stresses of the small scale magnetic fields, instead of the large scale organized magnetic fields.

(1) the viscoelastic stresses due to the small-scale magnetic field can drive a jet-like outflow in a protostellar system; and (2) the jet velocity scales with the turbulent magnetic field strength and with the inverse of the magnetic Prandtl number.
the mean-field Maxwell stresses in MRI-driven turbulence can be approximated by a viscoelastic fluid and that this approximation can be used to explain jets in astrophysical systems.
